questions.stem:
In a company the 200 employees are classified as full-time workers, part-time workers or contractors.
The table below shows the number of employees in each category and whether they walk to work or use some form of transport.

$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|}\hline & \text{Walk} & \text{Transport}\\\hline \text{Full-time worker} & 2 & 8\\\hline \text{Part-time worker} & 35 & 75\\\hline \text{Contractor} & 30 & 50\\\hline\end{array}$

The events $F$, $H$ and $C$ are that an employee is a full-time worker, part-time worker or contractor respectively. Let $W$ be the event that an employee walks to work.

An employee is selected at random.

Find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: for denominator of 200 and attempt to add $2+8$ or $35+75$ or $30+50$; A1: for $0.55$ or exact equivalent fraction e.g. $\frac{11}{20}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Correct answers only score full marks for each part. If a probability is not in [0, 1] award M0
- $\frac{35+75}{200}=0.55$ M1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: for a fully correct expression (e.g. $1-0.01$); A1: for $0.99$ or an exact equivalent fraction
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\frac{200-2}{200}=0.99$ M1 A1

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $\left[\mathrm{P}(W\mid C)\right]=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(W\cap C)}{\mathrm{P}(C)}=\dfrac{30/200}{80/200}=\dfrac{30}{80}=0.375$. M1: for a correct ratio or a correct formula and at least one correct prob (i.e. a correct num or denom). BUT award M0 if num is $\mathrm{P}(W)\times\mathrm{P}(C)=\frac{67}{200}\times\frac{80}{200}$ or if num $>$ denom; A1: for $0.375$ or $3/8$ or any exact equivalent.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Let $B$ be the event that an employee uses the bus.
Given that 10% of full-time workers use the bus, 30% of part-time workers use the bus and 20% of contractors use the bus,

(d) draw a Venn diagram to represent the events $F$, $H$, $C$ and $B$,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) M1: for a box and the 3 regions $F$, $C$ and $H$ labelled or implied and single set $B$ labelled. There should be no intersections between $F$, $C$ and $H$ unless marked by zeros. They may have 3 circles for $F$, $C$ and $B$ with $H = F' \cap C'$ etc. Condone lack of zero in the given diagram. B1: for the 9 and 1 or 0.045 and 0.005 (o.e.) in the correct regions ($F$); B1: for the 77 and 33 or 0.385 and 0.165 (o.e.) in the correct regions ($H$); B1: for the 64 and 16 or 0.32 and 0.08 (o.e.) in the correct regions ($C$). Allow diagrams with intersections between $F$, $C$ and $H$ provided these are marked with 0. If their diagram indicates extra empty regions do not treat a blank as 0. May have $B$ in 3 bits that are disconnected.

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) find the probability that a randomly selected employee uses the bus to travel to work.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (e) $\dfrac{1+16+33}{200}=0.25$. M1: for a numerator made up of their $1+$ their $16+$ their $33$ and a denom of 200 and num $<200$ (also allow sum of their probabilities provided sum $<1$); A1: for $0.25$ or any exact equivalent.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Time (minutes) } t & 11-20 & 21-25 & 26-30 & 31-35 & 36-45 & 46-60\\\hline \text{Number of students } f & 62 & 88 & 16 & 13 & 11 & 10\\\hline\end{array}$

[You may use $\sum ft^2 = 134281.25$]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Estimate the mean and standard deviation of these data.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Correct answers only score full marks. B1: for $\sum ft = 4837.5$ (allow 4838 or 4840); M1: for attempt at their $\dfrac{\sum ft}{\sum f}$; Mean $=\dfrac{"4837.5"}{200}$, A1: awrt $24.2$ or $\frac{387}{16}$; M1: for correct expression including square root seen, $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{134281.25}{200}-\left(\dfrac{4837.5}{200}\right)^2}=9.293\ldots$ (accept $s=9.32$); A1: awrt $9.29$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Correct answers only score full marks in each part except (c)
- If no $\sum ft$ seen (or attempt at $\sum ft$ seen), B1 can be implied by a correct mean of awrt 24.2
- allow 1sf so $\sum f$ = awrt 200 and $\sum ft$ = awrt 5000. Or award M1 for a clear attempt at mean where at least 4 correct products of $\sum ft$ are seen
- Follow through their mean. Allow a transcription error in 134281.25 but not an incorrect re-calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the value of the median.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) M1: for a correct fraction $\times 5$, ignore end point but must be $+$ (allow use of $(n+1)$ giving 100.5...); $Q_2=\left[20.5\right]+\dfrac{(100/100.5-62)}{88}\times5=22.659\ldots$, A1: awrt $22.7$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Show that the estimated value of the lower quartile is 18.6 to 3 significant figures.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1cso: for a fully correct expression including end point. NB Answer is given. $Q_1=10.5+\dfrac{(50/50.25)}{62}\times10\left[=18.56\right]$ (*). Allow use of $(n+1)$ giving 50.25... but use of 50.5 scores B0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ($n$ + 1 gives 18.604…)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Estimate the interquartile range of this distribution.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1: for $Q_3=25.5$ (or awrt 25.7 using $n+1$); B1ft: for their $Q_3-$ their $Q_1$ (or 18.6) (provided $>0$), accept awrt 2sf; IQR $=6.9$ (use of $n+1$ gives $7.1$). Correct answer only scores 2/2.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $Q_3$= 25.5 (Use of $n$ + 1 gives 25.734…)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Give a reason why the mean and standard deviation are not the most appropriate summary statistics to use with these data.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (e) B1: Must mention that the data is skewed or not symmetrical. Do not award for "outliers". The data is skewed (condone "negative skew").

parts.label: f
parts.text:
The person timing the exam made an error and each student actually took 5 minutes less than the times recorded above. The table below summarises the actual times.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Time (minutes) } t & 6-15 & 16-20 & 21-25 & 26-30 & 31-40 & 41-55\\\hline \text{Number of students } f & 62 & 88 & 16 & 13 & 11 & 10\\\hline\end{array}$

(f) Without further calculations, explain the effect this would have on each of the estimates found in parts (a), (b), (c) and (d).
(3)

questions.stem:
The weight, in grams, of beans in a tin is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation 7.8

Given that 10% of tins contain less than 200 g, find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Let $X$ be the amount of beans in a tin. $\mathrm{P}(X<200)=0.1$. M1: for an attempt to standardise (allow $\pm$) with 200 and 7.8 and set $=\pm$ any $z$ value ($|z|>1$); B1: for $z=\pm1.2816$ (or better used as a $z$) [may be implied by 209.996(102...) or better seen]; $\dfrac{200-\mu}{7.8}=-1.2816$, $\mu=209.996\ldots$, A1: awrt $210$. The 210 must follow from correct working — sign scores A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone poor handling of notation if answers are correct but A marks must have correct working.
- [ calc gives 1.28155156…]
- A1 for awrt 210 (can be scored for using 1.28 but then they get M1B0A1)
- If answer is awrt 210 and 209.996… or better seen then award M1B1A1
- $z$ = 1.28 gives 209.984 and $z$ = 1.282 gives 209.9996 and both score M1B0A1
- If answer is awrt 210 or awrt 209.996 then award M1B0A1 (unless of course $z$ = 1.2816 is seen)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the percentage of tins that contain more than 225 g of beans.
